description: Power Converter Practical - dual bridge rectifier stage feeding a switching/PWM regulated output stage
_meta_note: Node numbers below are taken directly from frontend/assets/socket_positions_power_converter.json. Group wiring (correct_groups/group_metadata) reflects the labelled board layout (INPUT AC SUPPLY, two diamond diode bridges, SWITCHING PULSE header, and 9V/12V/+5V/GND/+12V output rail) visible on the trainer silkscreen. VERIFY expected node groupings against your actual trainer manual before treating this as ground truth, and edit any group_metadata entry that doesn't match your hardware.
aim: To construct the Power Converter circuit (dual bridge rectifier stage plus switching regulator stage), observe the rectified and regulated DC output, and verify the output rails against the expected voltages.
objective: Understand how two diode-bridge rectifier stacks convert the AC input into pulsating DC.
Understand how the switching/PWM stage regulates the rectified DC into stable output rails.
Measure and verify the 9V, 12V, +5V and +12V output rails against expected values.
Identify the effect of a missing or wrongly connected diode/switching-pulse link on the output.
theory: The Power Converter board takes AC input and rectifies it using two full-wave diode bridge stacks (each built from four diodes arranged in a diamond configuration), producing pulsating DC. This pulsating DC feeds a switching stage, controlled via the SWITCHING PULSE header, which chops and regulates the rectified DC into stable low-voltage output rails (9V, 12V, +5V, +12V) referenced to a common GND. The switching stage improves efficiency over a purely linear regulator by rapidly switching the pass element on and off and filtering the result, rather than dissipating the voltage difference as heat.
working_principle: AC input enters at the INPUT AC SUPPLY terminals and is fed into both diode bridge stacks in parallel/series as wired by the student. Each bridge converts its half of the AC waveform into pulsating DC using the same diagonal-pair diode conduction principle as a standard bridge rectifier. The combined rectified DC is then routed to the SWITCHING PULSE stage, which uses a control pulse to regulate the output into the 9V/12V/+5V/+12V rails. GND provides the common return path for all measurements. A missing or wrong diode connection in either bridge breaks that bridge's rectification path, reducing the DC feeding the switching stage and degrading or destabilizing the regulated output rails.
apparatus: AC input supply (as specified by the board rating)
8 x diodes forming the two bridge stacks (4 per bridge)
Dual channel CRO / Oscilloscope with probes

components.role: Supplies the AC input to both diode bridge stacks.

components.role: First full-wave diode bridge; rectifies AC into pulsating DC.

components.name: Bridge Stack B (bottom)
components.role: Second full-wave diode bridge; rectifies AC into pulsating DC.

components.name: Switching Pulse Stage

procedure: Switch off the AC mains supply before making or changing any connections.
Wire the AC input terminals to the first diode bridge stack, following the diode orientation markings.
Wire the AC input terminals to the second diode bridge stack, following the diode orientation markings.
Connect the switching pulse header as per the trainer wiring table.
Connect the multimeter/CRO to the desired output rail (9V, 12V, +5V, +12V) and GND.
Switch on the AC supply and observe/measure the output waveform and voltage.
Repeat for each output rail as required by the practical.
precautions: Always switch off the AC mains supply before making or changing any connections.
Ensure diodes in both bridge stacks are connected with correct polarity.
Do not exceed the rated voltage/current of the diodes or switching stage.
Use an isolation transformer and avoid direct contact with mains-side wiring.
Set the multimeter to the correct range (DC voltage) before measuring any output rail.
Double check all connections against the wiring/group table before switching on the supply.
Keep CRO probes properly grounded and set to the correct volts/division before observing waveforms.
expected_output: Regulated DC present on the 9V, 12V, +5V and +12V output rails referenced to GND, derived from the rectified and switched AC input.
expected_voltage: Output rails should read close to their labelled nominal values (9V, 12V, +5V, +12V) at GND reference, subject to load and input supply tolerance.
expected_waveforms: Input: Sinusoidal AC waveform at the AC input terminals.
Post-bridge (pre-switching): Full-wave rectified pulsating DC from each bridge stack.
Output rails: Smoothed/regulated DC with minimal ripple after the switching stage.
applications: DC power rails for embedded/control electronics
advantages: Higher efficiency than a purely linear regulator due to the switching stage.
Provides multiple regulated output rails from a single AC input.
disadvantages: More complex wiring than a single bridge rectifier.
Switching stage can introduce noise/ripple if not filtered correctly.

troubleshooting.symptom: No output voltage on any rail.
troubleshooting.likely_cause: Open diode in a bridge stack, broken AC input connection, or missing switching pulse link.
troubleshooting.fix: Check continuity of the AC input path and both diode bridges; verify the switching pulse header connection.

troubleshooting.symptom: One bridge stack shows only half-wave-like output.
troubleshooting.likely_cause: One diode in that bridge is missing, open, or wrongly oriented.
troubleshooting.fix: Identify the affected diode and reconnect it with correct polarity.

troubleshooting.symptom: Output rail voltage much lower or unstable.
troubleshooting.likely_cause: Switching pulse stage not correctly wired, or excessive loading on that rail.
troubleshooting.fix: Recheck the switching pulse connection and the specific output rail wiring against the group table.

common_mistakes: Reversing diode polarity in one of the bridge stacks.
Missing the switching pulse header connection.
Measuring an output rail without a proper GND reference.

viva_questions.question: Why does the Power Converter board use two diode bridge stacks instead of one?
viva_questions.reference_answer: To rectify the AC input in parallel or provide separate rectified DC feeds for different sections of the switching stage, increasing current handling and rail flexibility.

viva_questions.question: What is the role of the switching pulse stage?
viva_questions.reference_answer: It regulates the rectified DC into stable output rails by rapidly switching the pass element on and off, improving efficiency compared to a linear regulator.

viva_questions.question: What happens if a diode in one bridge stack is open?
viva_questions.reference_answer: That bridge degrades to half-wave-like rectification, reducing the DC feeding the switching stage and potentially destabilizing the regulated output rails.

viva_questions.question: Why is GND used as the common reference for all output rail measurements?
viva_questions.reference_answer: All regulated rails (9V, 12V, +5V, +12V) are referenced to the same ground, so a single common GND point ensures consistent, comparable voltage measurements.

g1.component_name: Bridge Stack A - AC Input / Diode branch (top-left leg)
g1.purpose: Routes AC input through the first diode of Bridge Stack A into the top bridge junction.
g1.description: Part of Bridge Stack A's rectification path from the AC input terminal into the top diamond bridge junction.
g1.effect_if_missing: Bridge Stack A loses part of its conduction path, degrading its rectified output for the corresponding half-cycle.
g1.effect_if_wrong: Reversed polarity on this leg can prevent conduction or risk excessive current during one half-cycle.
g1.next_step: Verify diode orientation on this leg and confirm nodes 2, 13, 14 and 6 are connected as per the wiring table.

g2.component_name: Bridge Stack A - AC Input / Diode branch (top-right leg)
g2.purpose: Routes AC input through the second diode of Bridge Stack A into the top bridge junction.
g2.description: Completing leg of Bridge Stack A's rectification path.
g2.effect_if_missing: Bridge Stack A loses part of its conduction path for the opposite half-cycle, reducing rectified output.
g2.effect_if_wrong: Reversed polarity on this leg can prevent conduction or risk diode damage.
g2.next_step: Verify diode orientation on this leg and confirm nodes 3, 7, 8 and 31 are connected as per the wiring table.

g3.component_name: Bridge Stack B - Diode branch (bottom-left leg)
g3.purpose: Routes current through the first diode of Bridge Stack B into the bottom bridge junction.
g3.description: Part of Bridge Stack B's rectification path.
g3.effect_if_missing: Bridge Stack B loses part of its conduction path, degrading its rectified output.
g3.effect_if_wrong: Reversed polarity on this leg can prevent conduction or risk diode damage.
g3.next_step: Verify diode orientation on this leg and confirm nodes 1, 6, 32 and 11 are connected as per the wiring table.

g4.component_name: Bridge Stack B - Diode branch (bottom-right leg)
g4.purpose: Routes current through the second diode of Bridge Stack B into the bottom bridge junction.
g4.description: Completing leg of Bridge Stack B's rectification path.
g4.effect_if_missing: Bridge Stack B loses part of its conduction path for the opposite half-cycle, reducing rectified output.
g4.effect_if_wrong: Reversed polarity on this leg can prevent conduction or risk diode damage.
g4.next_step: Verify diode orientation on this leg and confirm nodes 4, 9, 10 and 33 are connected as per the wiring table.

g5.component_name: Bridge Stack A - Internal bridge junction link
g5.purpose: Connects the shared internal junction nodes of Bridge Stack A.
g5.description: Internal tie point joining the two halves of Bridge Stack A into a single rectifier bridge.
g5.effect_if_missing: Bridge Stack A cannot form a complete bridge, so no proper DC output is produced from this stack.
g5.effect_if_wrong: An incorrect junction link can short the AC input or disable rectification for this stack.
g5.next_step: Confirm nodes 3, 30 and 31 are correctly tied together per the wiring table.

g6.component_name: Bridge Stack B - Internal bridge junction link
g6.purpose: Connects the shared internal junction nodes of Bridge Stack B.
g6.description: Internal tie point joining the two halves of Bridge Stack B into a single rectifier bridge.
g6.effect_if_missing: Bridge Stack B cannot form a complete bridge, so no proper DC output is produced from this stack.
g6.effect_if_wrong: An incorrect junction link can short the input or disable rectification for this stack.
g6.next_step: Confirm nodes 5, 32 and 33 are correctly tied together per the wiring table.

g7.purpose: Connects the rectified DC output to the 9V and 12V labelled output terminals.
g7.description: Output rail tie point for the lower-left 9V/12V terminal block.
g7.effect_if_missing: The 9V/12V rail will show no reading or an unstable/floating reading.
g7.effect_if_wrong: Miswiring this group can short the output or deliver the wrong voltage to the 9V/12V terminals.
g7.next_step: Confirm nodes 23, 24, 17 and 18 are wired to the 9V/12V output block as per the wiring table.

g8.component_name: Switching Pulse / GND Output Rail Group
g8.purpose: Connects the switching pulse output stage to the GND-referenced output terminals.
g8.description: Ties the switching stage output to the GND-referenced terminal group used for measurement.
g8.effect_if_missing: The switching stage output cannot be measured correctly; readings may float or show zero.
g8.effect_if_wrong: Miswiring this group can short the switching output or give an incorrect reading.
g8.next_step: Confirm nodes 19, 20, 27 and 28 are wired as per the wiring table.
